sections.h2: What are my options for selling a house in Cibolo, Texas?
sections.html:
Cibolo homeowners can sell three ways: through an agent listing, on their own, or to a buyer who pays cash and takes the house as-is. The best fit depends on how much repair work the house needs and how soon you must close.

  • Agent listing: reaches the widest group of buyers, but you wait on showings, a buyer's loan and an appraisal.
  • For sale by owner: saves the agent's role and adds your own paperwork and negotiation.
  • Cash sale as-is: removes repair requests and the loan step, which helps with inherited houses, rentals and sales under time pressure.

A few Cibolo details shape any route: the city's place east of San Antonio, a county line that runs nearby, and a permit office that runs through one online portal.

sections.h2: Where is Cibolo and how did the city grow?
sections.html:
Cibolo lies in the extreme western corner of Guadalupe County, along FM 78 and FM 1103, with Interstate 10 to the south and Interstate 35 to the north, about 13 miles east of the San Antonio metropolitan area, according to the city's own history page. The city places itself in the Metrocom, the northeast corner of Bexar County and southwest corner of Guadalupe County, with Schertz, Universal City, Selma, Live Oak, Garden Ridge, Converse and Kirby as neighbors. Randolph Air Force Base, a pilot training facility, is nearby.

The name is an Indian word for buffalo, and the town took the name of the creek. The city says its story begins in 1876, when the Southern Pacific Railroad came through and linked the farms to Houston and San Antonio. Cotton was the main cash crop for decades, along with corn, wheat, oats and milo maize. Cibolo voted to become an independent township on October 9, 1965.

The city's census figures show the scale of the change: 440 people in 1970, 1,757 in 1990, 3,035 in 2000, 19,580 in 2010 after a challenge to the count, and an estimated 37,061 as of 2023.

sections.h2: Does Cibolo property sit in Bexar County or Guadalupe County?
sections.html:
The city's text puts Cibolo in Guadalupe County and describes the surrounding Metrocom as reaching into northeast Bexar County. That means your tax bill and appraisal district depend on the exact parcel, and you should read it before you set a price.

Texas appraisal districts value property as of January 1 and send notices in spring. The Comptroller says a tax lien attaches on January 1, bills are mailed around October 1, and unpaid balances turn delinquent on February 1, when a six percent penalty and one percent interest are added. Penalty then grows by one percent a month until July 1, when it reaches 12 percent. A private attorney hired by a taxing unit can add up to 20 percent more.

The state also lets owners aged 65 or over, disabled owners and disabled veterans pay in installments and, in some cases, qualifies them for ceilings or exemptions. Ask the county tax office, not an online estimator, for your balance and the current adopted rates.

sections.h2: What does Cibolo's permit office handle, and how does it affect a sale?
sections.html:
The Cibolo Building and Permitting Department handles permits and inspections, and it asks everyone to apply through the MGO Connect portal. The department is at 201 West Loop 539, and its main office number is (210) 658-4175.

For a seller, the practical step is to find any permit tied to your address and see whether it was closed. The city's portal lets you look up a permit, and the office email is permitting@cibolotx.gov. A deck, a pool, a new water heater, a patio cover or an addition without a final inspection is the kind of item that holds up a title company or a buyer's inspector.

sections.h2: What building codes and inspection rules apply to repairs in Cibolo?
sections.html:
Cibolo adopted the 2021 editions of the International Building, Residential, Energy Conservation, Plumbing, Fuel Gas, Mechanical, Swimming Pool and Spa, and Fire Codes, together with the 2023 National Electrical Code, under Ordinance 1475. Local amendments are listed on the city's Codes and Fees pages.

The city states a few working rules for permit holders:

  • Contractors must register before they submit a permit application.
  • An account in the portal is required before any application.
  • Permits, inspections and permit lookups all run through the same portal.

If you plan repairs before selling, ask the office whether the work needs a permit. If you plan to sell as-is, tell the buyer about unfinished work in writing.

sections.h2: How does a homestead exemption affect a Cibolo sale?
sections.html:
A Cibolo owner who lives in the house can claim the Texas residence homestead exemption, and the buyer needs to file a new application after closing. School districts must give a $140,000 exemption on a residence homestead, and the Comptroller says any taxing unit may adopt a local option exemption of up to 20 percent of value, with a floor of $5,000.

An owner who is 65 or older or disabled gets an extra $60,000 school exemption and a ceiling on school taxes that can follow the owner to a new Texas homestead, in proportion. For a seller moving within Texas, that transfer detail is worth asking about. Appraised value for a homestead may not rise more than 10 percent a year, per the Comptroller.

sections.h2: How do I record a deed for a Cibolo house?
sections.html:
The deed goes to the clerk of the county where the land lies, and the clerk's Texas manual says the document must be signed and acknowledged before a notary or another authorized officer. Filing costs begin at $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, with added records management, archive and technology fees.

Your title company handles recording after funding. Bring a payoff letter for any loan, your photo ID and, if the seller is an estate, the court order or other paper that proves authority to sell.

sections.h2: What if my Cibolo house is in probate, has a tenant or is near foreclosure?
sections.html:
Texas law sets short windows for each, so start with the paperwork.

  • Probate: a will is probated within four years of death unless the court accepts a later filing for good reason. Heirs may transfer property by an affidavit of heirship filed with the county clerk, but no law makes a title company accept it.
  • Tenant: the notice to vacate is at least 3 days unless the lease says otherwise, and the writ of possession cannot issue earlier than 6 days after judgment.
  • Foreclosure: the sale is a public auction at the courthouse, on the first Tuesday of the month, between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. If a deficiency suit follows, it must be filed within two years of the sale.

If your house has two or more of these, a cash buyer can often work around them, but the title company will still need paperwork showing who has authority to sign.

faqs.a: The city's own history page places Cibolo in the extreme western corner of Guadalupe County, and says the surrounding Metrocom area covers northeast Bexar County. Check your tax statement to see which appraisal district holds your parcel.

faqs.q: How do I check for an open permit on my Cibolo house?
faqs.a: Use the MGO Connect portal, which has a permit lookup, or contact permitting@cibolotx.gov or (210) 658-4175. Closing any open permit before you list helps the sale move.

faqs.q: Which building codes does Cibolo enforce?
faqs.a: Cibolo enforces the 2021 International codes and the 2023 National Electrical Code under Ordinance 1475. The Codes and Fees section of the city site lists the local amendments.

faqs.q: When do Texas property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: Property taxes become delinquent on February 1 if unpaid by the end of January, per the Texas Comptroller. A six percent penalty plus one percent interest is added at that point.

faqs.q: Can heirs sell a Cibolo house without full probate?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A muniment of title or a small estate affidavit can work when the estate qualifies and a court approves, but each has limits. A probate attorney can confirm which route fits your family.
